name: AD — Member Added to a Privileged (Tier-0) Group
description:
Attacker objective
Gain domain dominance or persistence by adding an account to a highly-privileged group (Domain/Enterprise/Schema Admins, built-in Operators, or privileged Exchange groups).

Attack logic
Membership changes to Tier-0 groups are rare and among the most consequential directory changes. An addition to these groups grants far-reaching control and warrants verification.

Why this detection works
Group-membership events (4728/4756/4732) record the group, the added member and the acting subject.

False positives
Authorised administration.

Tuning
Correlate with change tickets; the local Administrators group can be noisier and can be split out if needed.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 4728/4756/4732 (TargetUserName/group, MemberName, SubjectUserName).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SubjectUserName added a member to a Tier-0 group; MemberName = who was added.
2. Verify authorisation; if unauthorised, remove the member and investigate the subject and the added account's subsequent activity.
query: event.code:("4728" or "4756" or "4732") and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName:("Domain Admins" or "Enterprise Admins" or "Schema Admins" or "Group Policy Creator Owners" or "DnsAdmins" or "Cert Publishers" or "Exchange Organization Administrators" or "Exchange Trusted Subsystem" or "Account Operators" or "Backup Operators" or "Server Operators" or "Administrators")
